title: 343: Oppenheimer: The Father of the Atom Bomb (Part 1)

sentences.en: All of a sudden, the night turned into day, and it was tremendously bright.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，黑夜变成了白昼，光芒万丈。

sentences.en: The chill turned into warmth.
sentences.zh: 寒意转为暖意。

sentences.en: The fireball gradually turned from white to yellow to red as it grew in size and climbed into the sky.
sentences.zh: 火球在升入天空的过程中，体积不断增大，颜色也逐渐从白色变为黄色，再变为红色。

sentences.en: After about five seconds, the darkness returned, but with the sky and the air filled with a purple glow, just as though we were surrounded by an aurora borealis.
sentences.zh: 大约五秒钟后，黑暗重新降临，但天空和空气中弥漫着紫色的光芒，仿佛我们被北极光包围了一样。

sentences.en: We stood there in awe as the blast wave picked up chunks of dirt from the desert soil and soon passed us by.
sentences.zh: 我们敬畏地站在那里，看着冲击波卷起沙漠地表的泥土，很快从我们身边掠过。

sentences.en: That was Joe Hirschfeld, who was a chemist who'd been assigned to measure the radioactive fallout from the test on the first atom bomb dropped on the 16th of July, 1945.
sentences.zh: 那是乔·赫什菲尔德（Joe Hirschfeld），他是一位化学家，被指派负责测量1945年7月16日第一颗原子弹试验产生的放射性尘埃。

sentences.en: And Dominic, we are thinking about the birth of the atom bomb, the Manhattan Project, all that malarkey.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我们正在思考原子弹的诞生、曼哈顿计划，以及所有那些胡言乱语。

sentences.en: Malarkey, very good.
sentences.zh: 胡言乱语，说得好。

sentences.en: Well, it's such a sombre and kind of overwhelming subject, isn't it, that one wants to perhaps introduce, slightly puncture the gravity of it, because otherwise it's so depressing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个如此沉重且令人难以承受的话题，不是吗？人们或许想介绍一下，稍微冲淡一下它的严肃性，否则太压抑了。

sentences.en: And we're doing this obviously because there's a new film out about the life of the man often described as the godfather
sentences.zh: 我们之所以这么做，显然是因为有一部关于那个常被称为“教父”的人的生平的新电影上映了，

sentences.en: of the atom bomb, Oppenheimer, who, and I know so little about Oppenheimer, I don't even know what his first name is, I just suddenly realised.
sentences.zh: 原子弹之父，奥本海默。我对奥本海默知之甚少，我甚至不知道他的名字是什么，我突然意识到这一点。

sentences.en: His name is J.
sentences.zh: 他的名字是J。

sentences.en: Robert Oppenheimer, Tom.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·奥本海默，汤姆。

sentences.en: So what's the J, though?
sentences.zh: 那么J代表什么呢？

sentences.en: Julius.
sentences.zh: 朱利叶斯。

sentences.en: So his father was called Julius.
sentences.zh: 所以他父亲叫朱利叶斯。

sentences.en: We'll come on to his parents in a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我们待会儿再谈他的父母。

sentences.en: And by the way, for those people listening, that's the first test, that's the Trinity test in New Mexico.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，对于听众朋友们，那是第一次试验，即新墨西哥州的“三位一体”试验。

sentences.en: And so the bomb wasn't dropped, it was sort of installed, and then they do the detonation there.
sentences.zh: 所以炸弹并没有被投下，而是被安装在那里，然后他们在那里进行了引爆。

sentences.en: Is that in the hut?
sentences.zh: 是在那个小屋里吗？

sentences.en: Yes, they're exactly, they're all miles away.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错，他们都在几英里外。

sentences.en: That they have in the fourth Indiana Jones film.
sentences.zh: 那是他们在第四部《夺宝奇兵》电影里演的那样。

sentences.en: Do they?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: I think they do.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: You've been watching a lot of Indiana Jones, Tom, haven't you?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你最近看了很多《夺宝奇兵》，对吧？

sentences.en: Because you're gearing up for a mighty series.
sentences.zh: 因为你正在为一部宏大的系列片做准备。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's coming next week, so we mustn't get distracted by that.
sentences.zh: 没错，下周就要播了，所以我们不能被那个分心。

sentences.en: I vaguely remember.
sentences.zh: 我隐约记得。

sentences.en: Anyway, listen, we don't want to be talking about Indiana Jones, or if you're talking about Julius, as I don't know who he's called.
sentences.zh: 总之，听着，我们不想谈论《夺宝奇兵》，或者如果你在谈论朱利叶斯，因为我不知道他叫什么。

sentences.en: Well, Robert, he was called Robert Oppenheimer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，罗伯特，他叫罗伯特·奥本海默。

sentences.en: And Oppenheimer is, so the film, the Christopher Nolan film, is inspired by a book, which on the Pulitzer Prize, called American Prometheus, by Kai Bird and Martin J.
sentences.zh: 奥本海默，所以这部电影，克里斯托弗·诺兰的电影，灵感来源于一本书，那本书获得了普利策奖，叫《美国普罗米修斯》，作者是凯·伯德和马丁·J。

sentences.en: Sherwin.
sentences.zh: 舍温。

sentences.en: And American Prometheus, that will appeal to you, Tom, because, of course, Prometheus is the fellow who, he steals fire and brings it from Zeus as a gift to mankind, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 《美国普罗米修斯》，这会吸引你的，汤姆，因为普罗米修斯当然就是那个偷走火种，并从宙斯那里把它作为礼物带给人类的人，不是吗？

sentences.en: But then is punished for it.
sentences.zh: 但随后却因此受到了惩罚。

sentences.en: So what happens to Prometheus?
sentences.zh: 那么普罗米修斯发生了什么？

sentences.en: He gets chained to a rock in the Caucasus Mountains, and either an eagle or a vulture, depending on the myth, comes and rips out his guts, and then they grow back,
sentences.zh: 他被锁在高加索山脉的一块岩石上，根据神话的不同，要么是一只老鹰，要么是一只秃鹫，过来掏出他的内脏，然后内脏又长出来，

sentences.en: and then next day, the eagle or straight vulture comes back and does the same.
sentences.zh: 第二天，那只老鹰或秃鹫又回来做同样的事。

sentences.en: And so it goes on, until finally Heracles comes and shoots the eagle or straight vulture.
sentences.zh: 就这样一直持续下去，直到最后赫拉克勒斯过来射杀了那只老鹰或秃鹫。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But that idea of somebody who has stolen something that is at once exciting, invigorating, liberating, but also utterly terrifying, which is fire,
sentences.zh: 但那种偷走某种东西的想法，它既令人兴奋、振奋、解放，又极其可怕，那就是火，

sentences.en: and taking something that should properly belong to the gods and giving it to human beings, and then is punished for it, and then becomes a kind of martyr.
sentences.zh: 把本应属于神的东西拿走并交给人类，然后因此受到惩罚，最后成为一种殉道者。

sentences.en: That's the core of Oppenheimer's story.
sentences.zh: 这就是奥本海默故事的核心。

sentences.en: I mean, the ancient myth that Oppenheimer himself famously invokes is from the Mahabharata, the great Indian epic, and specifically the Bhagavad Gita.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，奥本海默本人著名地引用的古老神话来自伟大的印度史诗《摩诃婆罗多》，特别是《薄伽梵歌》。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it's traditionally said that he sees the atom bomb, and he says, he quotes the Bhagavad Gita, now I am become death, the destroyer of worlds.
sentences.zh: 传统上说，他看到原子弹爆炸时，引用了《薄伽梵歌》中的话：“现在我成了死神，世界的毁灭者。”

sentences.en: But didn't he actually, he actually quoted a couple of lines, if the radiance of a thousand suns were to burst at once
sentences.zh: 但他实际上引用了几行诗，如果一千个太阳的光芒同时在天空中爆发，

sentences.en: into the sky, that would be like the splendor of the mighty one.
sentences.zh: 那将如同万能者的光辉。

sentences.en: So in those two quotes, both of which I've seen attributed to him, on the one hand, there's the sense of death, and on the other, there's the sense of radiance and light.
sentences.zh: 所以在这两句引语中，我都见过有人将其归于他名下，一方面是死亡的感觉，另一方面是光芒和光明的感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the ambivalence, by the way, is at the centre of his relationship with the atom bomb, and with the nuclear age, and the Cold War, and all those kinds of things,
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这种矛盾心理是他与原子弹、核时代、冷战以及所有这些事物关系的核心，

sentences.en: as we'll go on to discuss.
sentences.zh: 正如我们接下来要讨论的那样。

sentences.en: And actually, the stories that are told about him, the reason we didn't start with that story is, I don't think he did say that, because he claims later that he said it,
sentences.zh: 事实上，关于他的故事，我们没有从那个故事开始的原因是，我不认为他真的说过那句话，因为他后来声称他说了，

sentences.en: but people at the time don't recall him saying it.
sentences.zh: 但当时在场的人并不记得他说过。

sentences.en: But I mean, he'd studied Sanskrit.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，他学过梵文。

sentences.en: I mean, we are talking about one of the cleverest men who seems ever to have lived.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们谈论的是有史以来最聪明的人之一。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a guy who turns up to the Netherlands not speaking Dutch and gives a lecture in Dutch.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这家伙去荷兰时不会说荷兰语，却用荷兰语做了一场讲座。

sentences.en: He did indeed.
sentences.zh: 他确实做到了。

sentences.en: I mean, he's an unbelievably clever guy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是一个极其聪明的人。

sentences.en: So maybe he muttered it in Sanskrit.
sentences.zh: 所以也许他用梵文嘟囔了那句话。

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: I think the truth of it is he said it to himself, he says he said it to himself, or he thought it.
sentences.zh: 我认为事实是他对自己说的，他说他对自己说了，或者他想到了。

sentences.en: I wonder whether there's a little bit of the Esprit d'Escalier there, you know, that sort of...
sentences.zh: 我不知道这是否有一点“楼梯间机智”的成分，你知道，那种……

sentences.en: It would have been great if I had said this, so I'll say that I did.
sentences.zh: 如果我说了这句话该多好，所以我说我说了。

sentences.en: But no, so the Oppenheimer story is not just the story of, as you say, one of the titanic intellects of the 20th century and somebody who,
sentences.zh: 但不是的，所以奥本海默的故事不仅仅是关于，正如你所说，20世纪最伟大的智者之一，以及某个人，

sentences.en: as you also said, is the godfather, or indeed the father of the atomic age.
sentences.zh: 正如你也说过的，是原子时代的教父，或者确实是父亲。

sentences.en: But it's also a kind of thriller, actually, Tom, because Oppenheimer becomes, in the 1950s, the supreme martyr, the sacrificial victim
sentences.zh: 但它实际上也是一种惊悚片，汤姆，因为奥本海默在20世纪50年代成为了至高无上的殉道者，成为了牺牲品，

sentences.en: in the McCarthyite anti-communist Red Scares hysteria of the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 在麦卡锡主义的反共“红色恐慌”歇斯底里中。

sentences.en: That's what makes his story such an exciting one.
sentences.zh: 这就是让他的故事如此激动人心的原因。

sentences.en: Because the context for that is, of course, that it's the United States that gets the atom bomb.
sentences.zh: 因为其背景当然是美国获得了原子弹。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But the United States is facing a rival superpower that is also after the atom bomb.
sentences.zh: 但美国正面临着一个同样在追求原子弹的超级大国对手。

sentences.en: And so the knowledge, this Promethean knowledge, is something very, very prized.
sentences.zh: 所以这种知识，这种普罗米修斯式的知识，是非常非常珍贵的。

sentences.en: Well, right from the start of the Manhattan Project, there was a sense of a race.
sentences.zh: 嗯，从曼哈顿计划一开始，就有一种竞赛感。

sentences.en: So initially, that race is against Nazi Germany.
sentences.zh: 所以最初，那场竞赛是针对纳粹德国的。

sentences.en: But then, as time goes on, that race starts to become a race for the Soviet Union, to stay ahead of the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，那场竞赛开始变成与苏联的竞赛，为了保持领先于苏联。

sentences.en: That becomes, you know, that sort of sense of urgency, that sense of tremendous excitement, is there throughout Oppenheimer's story.
sentences.zh: 那变成了，你知道，那种紧迫感，那种巨大的兴奋感，贯穿了奥本海默的故事。

sentences.en: So let's kick off, Tom, by talking about Oppenheimer himself, the man, because he is an extraordinary man.
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，让我们从谈论奥本海默本人开始吧，因为他是一个非凡的人。

sentences.en: He's born in April 1904, and he is the child of German-Jewish immigrants.
sentences.zh: 他出生于1904年4月，是德国犹太移民的孩子。

sentences.en: Actually, a lot of the people in this story will be of German-Jewish immigrant stock, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这个故事里的很多人实际上都是德国犹太移民后裔。

sentences.en: So they're ethnically and they're culturally Jewish, but they're not observant.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在种族和文化上是犹太人，但他们并不遵守宗教仪式。

sentences.en: They don't go to the synagogue or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 他们不去犹太教堂之类的场所。

sentences.en: His father, Julius, was born in Frankfurt.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲朱利叶斯出生于法兰克福。

sentences.en: He's a real autodidact.
sentences.zh: 他是一个真正的自学者。

sentences.en: He spends all his spare time going to art galleries in New York City and reading history books and things.
sentences.zh: 他把所有的空闲时间都花在去纽约市的艺术画廊和阅读历史书籍等事情上。

sentences.en: And he worked as a partner in a clothing firm, which sounds very unglamorous, but he's enormously rich.
sentences.zh: 他是一家服装公司的合伙人，这听起来很不光鲜，但他非常有钱。

sentences.en: Because he has three Van Goghs and a Picasso.
sentences.zh: 因为他有三幅梵高的画和一幅毕加索的画。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 他确实有。

sentences.en: And a Rembrandt, and a Renoir, and a Cezanne.
sentences.zh: 还有一幅伦勃朗、一幅雷诺阿和一幅塞尚。

sentences.en: So that's not bad, is it?
sentences.zh: 所以这还不错，不是吗？

sentences.en: This is very good going.
sentences.zh: 这非常不错。

sentences.en: And they live on the Upper West Side, I think, in New York City.
sentences.zh: 我想他们住在纽约市的上西区。

sentences.en: His wife is Ella Friedman.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子是埃拉·弗里德曼。

sentences.en: She's a painter.
sentences.zh: 她是一位画家。

sentences.en: She's also from a sort of German-Jewish immigrant stock.
sentences.zh: 她也来自某种德国犹太移民背景。

sentences.en: And they're very well off.
sentences.zh: 他们非常富有。

sentences.en: They have a summer house on Long Island where their little boy,
sentences.zh: 他们在长岛有一栋避暑别墅，他们的小男孩，

sentences.en: Robert, goes sailing.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特，在那里航海。

sentences.en: So in other words, they're not a sort of your Lower East Side, kind of struggling Jewish immigrant family, quite the reverse.
sentences.zh: 所以换句话说，他们不是那种下东区的、苦苦挣扎的犹太移民家庭，恰恰相反。

sentences.en: And not surprisingly, given that he's surrounded by very cerebral parents who spend all their time going to art galleries,
sentences.zh: 而且毫不奇怪，考虑到他被非常理性的父母所包围，他们把所有时间都花在去艺术画廊上，

sentences.en: Robert, their son, is a very clever little boy.
sentences.zh: 他们的儿子罗伯特是一个非常聪明的小男孩。

sentences.en: And his passions, so Kai Bird and Martin Sherwin tell us, were poetry, an unusual interest for somebody who's sort of, you know, 8, 9, 10 years old, reading and writing poetry,
sentences.zh: 据凯·伯德和马丁·舍温告诉我们，他的爱好是诗歌，对于一个8、9、10岁左右的孩子来说，阅读和写作诗歌是一种不同寻常的兴趣，

sentences.en: building things with blocks, which is a sign of, obviously, the scientific mentality, I suppose, the sort of patterns and construction and all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 用积木搭建东西，这显然是科学思维的标志，我想，那种模式、结构和所有这些东西。

sentences.en: And minerals, Tom.
sentences.zh: 还有矿物，汤姆。

sentences.en: So he loves collecting minerals.
sentences.zh: 你喜欢矿物吗？

sentences.en: Do you like minerals?
sentences.zh: 我更喜欢化石。

sentences.en: I prefer fossils.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我知道你很喜欢化石。

sentences.en: Well, I know you're big on fossils.
sentences.zh: 我不知道化石和矿物是否属于同一个世界。

sentences.en: I don't know whether fossils and minerals are part of the same world.
sentences.zh: 我想，是的。

sentences.en: I think, yeah.
sentences.zh: 算是地质宝藏吧，是的。

sentences.en: Kind of geological treasures, yeah.
sentences.zh: 你知道还有谁吗？

sentences.en: Do you know who else?
sentences.zh: 威尔弗雷德·欧文，那位战争诗人。

sentences.en: Wilfred Owen, the war poet.
sentences.zh: 他是一位狂热的矿物学家，如果这是那个词的话。

sentences.en: He was a massive mineralologist, if that's the word.
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: Was he?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道这一点。

sentences.en: Well, I did not know that.
sentences.zh: 所以他一定很享受他的战壕生活。

sentences.en: So he must have enjoyed his trench.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有诗歌。

sentences.en: Well, and also poetry.
sentences.zh: 所以他和奥本海默会相处得很好，汤姆。

sentences.en: So he and Oppenheimer would have gone on famously, Tom.
sentences.zh: 是的，但威尔弗雷德·欧文在理论物理学方面并不擅长，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, but Wilfred Owen wasn't great on theoretical physics, was he?
sentences.zh: 不太擅长，是的。

sentences.en: Not so good, no.
sentences.zh: 而且，当然，在奥本海默进入全盛时期时，他已经去世了。

sentences.en: And also, of course, was dead by the time that Oppenheimer entered his prime.
sentences.zh: 那会阻碍谈话的流畅性。

sentences.en: That would inhibit the flow of conversation.
sentences.zh: 确实会。

sentences.en: It would.
sentences.zh: 在他的整个职业生涯中，有一种政治理想主义的感觉，因为他的父母热衷于一种叫做“伦理文化协会”的东西，这实际上很迷人。

sentences.en: All through his career, there was a sense of political idealism because his parents were into this thing called the Ethical Culture Society, which is fascinating, actually.
sentences.zh: 所以它成立于1876年，是由一个叫菲利克斯·阿德勒的人在纽约市从改革派犹太教中创立的。

sentences.en: So that was founded in 1876, and it was founded out of reform Judaism in New York City by a guy called Felix Adler.
sentences.zh: 他说，这是未来的犹太教。

sentences.en: And he said, this is the Judaism of the future.
sentences.zh: 我们不会有任何祈祷。

sentences.en: We won't have any prayers.
sentences.zh: 我们不会有任何宗教仪式。

sentences.en: We won't have any religious rituals.
sentences.zh: 这是一种犹太教的贵格会教派。

sentences.en: It's kind of Jewish Quakerism.
sentences.zh: 犹太贵格会。

sentences.en: Jewish Quakerism.
sentences.zh: 它非常强调社会福音。

sentences.en: It's very social gospel.
sentences.zh: 它非常注重善良和所有这类事情。

sentences.en: It's very about being kind and all that sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出为什么它会有吸引力，因为在某个时候，对于纽约那些有社会良知的富有犹太商人来说，有相当多的反犹太主义。

sentences.en: And you can see why it would appeal because there's a point when there's quite a lot of
sentences.zh: 这是一种方式……

sentences.en: anti-Semitism for basically rich Jewish businessmen in New York who have a social conscience.
sentences.zh: 这是一种同化主义的信条。

sentences.zh: 后来他去了德国的哥廷根，那是理论物理学的中心。

sentences.en: So as you said, Cambridge, you need to be good with test tubes.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，在剑桥，你得擅长摆弄试管。

sentences.en: This is experimental.
sentences.zh: 那是实验物理。

sentences.en: In Göttingen, it's all kind of more mathematical.
sentences.zh: 而在哥廷根，一切都更偏向数学化。

sentences.en: But there, he was so unpopular, interrupting in the class the whole time, that the other students boycotted the course unless he was removed.
sentences.zh: 但在那儿，他非常不受欢迎，总是打断课堂，以至于其他学生扬言，如果不把他赶走，他们就抵制这门课。

sentences.en: And was he?
sentences.zh: 那他被赶走了吗？

sentences.en: I think he was, or they found a way around it.
sentences.zh: 我想是的，或者他们找到了变通的方法。

sentences.en: But didn't he become friends with Werner Heisenberg?
sentences.zh: 但他不是和维尔纳·海森堡成了朋友吗？

sentences.en: Well, he's not really friends with Heisenberg, no.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他其实算不上是海森堡的朋友，不是。

sentences.en: But it's true that this is the point at which Werner Heisenberg…
sentences.zh: 但确实，正是在这个阶段，维尔纳·海森堡……

sentences.en: So Dominic, tell people who Werner Heisenberg is.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，给听众介绍一下维尔纳·海森堡是谁。

sentences.en: So Werner Heisenberg is Oppenheimer's kind of rival to some degree.
sentences.zh: 维尔纳·海森堡在某种程度上算是奥本海默的竞争对手。

sentences.en: He is one of the absolute meteoric figures of the golden age of breakthroughs in quantum physics, the high points of which is between 1925 and 1927.
sentences.zh: 他是量子物理学突破黄金时代中一颗耀眼的明星，那个时代的巅峰期在1925年到1927年之间。

sentences.en: And all these theoretical physics boffins are studying the movement of electrons around the nucleus of an atom, Tom, something I know you're very familiar with.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这些理论物理学的大牛们都在研究原子核周围电子的运动，这你应该很熟悉吧。

sentences.en: And of course Heisenberg, Tom, you will know this.
sentences.zh: 当然还有海森堡，汤姆，你肯定知道他。

sentences.en: Yeah, his uncertainty principle.
sentences.zh: 没错，他的不确定性原理。

sentences.en: Yeah, certainty principle.
sentences.zh: 没错，确定性原理。

sentences.en: So more precisely, the more exactly you know the position of a particle, Tom, the less, of course, you can predict its momentum.
sentences.zh: 更准确地说，汤姆，你对一个粒子的位置了解得越精确，当然，你就越无法预测它的动量。

sentences.en: You know that, don't you?
sentences.zh: 你知道这个，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, I did know that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我确实知道。

sentences.en: Incredibly exciting field.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极其令人兴奋的领域。

sentences.en: It's very much a young man's field.
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上是年轻人的领域。

sentences.en: So Einstein is kind of yesterday's man, really.
sentences.zh: 所以爱因斯坦其实已经算是过气人物了。

sentences.en: And all these young, thrusting young fellows are studying electrons and talking about waves and all this kind of business.
sentences.zh: 而这些年轻气盛的家伙们都在研究电子，谈论波之类的东西。

sentences.en: And Oppenheimer, he published 16 papers in three years.
sentences.zh: 奥本海默在三年内发表了16篇论文。

sentences.en: So he's a great kind of, you know, people know that he's an absolute star of this stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以他是个了不起的人，大家都知道他是这个领域的绝对明星。

sentences.en: Before coming on to do this, I did some research in the Bodleian.
sentences.zh: 在做这期节目之前，我在博德利图书馆做了一些研究。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Where I read that his achievements in physics include the
sentences.zh: 我在那儿读到，他在物理学上的成就包括……

sentences.en: Born-Oppenheimer approximation for molecular wave functions, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，是分子波函数的玻恩-奥本海默近似。

sentences.en: Well, wave functions is one of his things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，波函数确实是他的研究领域之一。

sentences.en: And field emissions, Tom.
sentences.zh: 还有场致发射，汤姆。

sentences.en: Did you read it?
sentences.zh: 你读到了吗？

sentences.en: But did Wikipedia tell you about his work on field emissions?
sentences.zh: 维基百科没告诉你他关于场致发射的研究吗？

sentences.en: No, it didn't.
sentences.zh: 没有，没提到。

sentences.en: But I was just wondering, I mean, what exactly is...
sentences.zh: 我只是在想，我是说，这到底是什么……

sentences.en: So tell the listeners what the approximation for molecular wave functions is all about?
sentences.zh: 那给听众讲讲什么是分子波函数近似吧？

sentences.en: I'll be very happy to do so.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意效劳。

sentences.en: But we'll be doing that, Tom, for members of the Rest is History Club.
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，我们要留给“历史余味”俱乐部的会员们讲。

sentences.en: You can sign up at restishistorypod.com.
sentences.zh: 你可以在restishistorypod.com注册。

sentences.en: Rest is particle physics.
sentences.zh: 余味是粒子物理学。

sentences.en: I don't want to waste it on the ordinary listeners.
sentences.zh: 我不想把它浪费在普通听众身上。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: No, that's fair enough.
sentences.zh: 不，这很公平。

sentences.en: So he gets a job, anyway, in the long run at the University of California at Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 总之，最终他在加州大学伯克利分校找到了一份工作。

sentences.en: And is he...
sentences.zh: 那他……

sentences.en: So Heisenberg is very much Germany's top boffin.
sentences.zh: 海森堡算是德国的顶级大牛。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Is Oppenheimer already been groomed to be America's top boffin?
sentences.zh: 奥本海默当时已经被培养成美国的顶级大牛了吗？

sentences.en: I don't think he's been groomed as the top boffin because there are lots of top boffins in America.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他被培养成“顶级大牛”，因为美国有很多顶级大牛。

sentences.en: But he's a top boffin.
sentences.zh: 但他确实是一位顶级大牛。

sentences.en: He is a top boffin, exactly.
sentences.zh: 他确实是，没错。

sentences.en: In the American Prometheus book, the Byrd and Sherwin book, they call him the Pied Piper of theoretical physics.
sentences.zh: 在伯德和舍温合著的《美国普罗米修斯》一书中，他们称他为理论物理学的“花衣魔笛手”。

sentences.en: So if you are clever and you are 18, you might well want to go and study with Oppenheimer.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你很聪明，而且才18岁，你很可能会想去跟奥本海默学习。

sentences.en: You'd go to what's called...
sentences.zh: 你会去那个所谓的……

sentences.en: So it's the Berkeley Radiation Lab, but it's actually nicknamed the Rad Lab.
sentences.zh: 那是伯克利辐射实验室，但昵称是“Rad Lab”。

sentences.en: And as we will see, that has another dimension, the Rad Lab.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将要看到的，这个“Rad Lab”还有另一层含义。

sentences.en: But just on Oppenheimer, before we get back to the rad element of the Rad Lab, he's still quite an awkward, lonely, cerebral man.
sentences.zh: 但回到奥本海默身上，在我们回到“Rad Lab”的“Rad”元素之前，他依然是个相当笨拙、孤独且理智的人。

sentences.en: The key question, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 关键问题来了，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Has he actually managed to speak to a woman at this point?
sentences.zh: 他这时候真的能和女性正常交流了吗？

sentences.en: I don't think so, really.
sentences.zh: 我觉得并没有。

sentences.en: He will do soon.
sentences.zh: 他很快就会了。

sentences.en: And a very important woman at that.
sentences.zh: 而且是一位非常重要的女性。

sentences.en: I heard, like, do you like electrons?
sentences.zh: 我听到的就像是，“你喜欢电子吗？”

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Is that how he speaks?
sentences.zh: 他就是这么说话的吗？

sentences.en: I imagine that's exactly how he speaks.
sentences.zh: 我想他说话就是这个样子。

sentences.en: Well, as you said, he does things like teaching himself Dutch.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如你所说，他会做一些自学荷兰语之类的事。

sentences.en: He spends all his time reading Sanskrit, reading sort of sacred texts, Hindu texts and things.
sentences.zh: 他把所有时间都花在阅读梵文、阅读各种神圣文本、印度教经文之类的东西上。

sentences.en: And then in the holidays, he goes off and he rides in New Mexico with his brother, Frank.
sentences.zh: 假期里，他会和弟弟弗兰克去新墨西哥州骑马。

sentences.en: They will ride a thousand miles in a summer, you know, across the kind of the plateaus and the valleys.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们夏天会骑行一千英里，穿过各种高原和山谷。

sentences.en: So he's not just a nerd?
sentences.zh: 所以他不仅仅是个书呆子？

sentences.en: No, but he's also not a man who would spend his summer lounging on a sofa with a gin and tonic.
sentences.zh: 不，但他也不是那种会整天躺在沙发上喝金汤力度过夏天的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So he wouldn't go to New Yorker.
sentences.zh: 所以他不会去《纽约客》那种地方。

sentences.en: He would not.
sentences.zh: 他不会的。

sentences.en: He's a very driven man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常有进取心的人。

sentences.en: Now, I said it was the Rad Lab.
sentences.zh: 刚才我说到了“Rad Lab”。

sentences.en: And when he gets to Berkeley, so we're in the sort of late 20s into the early and mid-1930s.
sentences.zh: 当他来到伯克利时，时间大概是20年代末到30年代初中期。

sentences.en: It's a real hotbed of radical politics.
sentences.zh: 那里是激进政治的温床。

sentences.en: So the Rad Lab is kind of double-edged.
sentences.zh: 所以“Rad Lab”这个名字有点双关。

sentences.en: And he goes to parties with other academics where they all talk about kind of Roosevelt's New Deal, about trade unions, about the rights of migrant farm workers,
sentences.zh: 他会和其他学者去参加聚会，大家都在谈论罗斯福的新政、工会、移民农场工人的权利，

sentences.en: all this sort of stuff that is absolutely in the air on the West Coast in the 30s.
sentences.zh: 所有这些在30年代的西海岸随处可见的话题。

sentences.en: I also read in the Bodleian that he claimed only to have heard about the Wall Street crash six months after it happened.
sentences.zh: 我还在博德利图书馆读到，他声称直到华尔街崩盘六个月后才听说这件事。

sentences.en: Well, that's very plausible.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这非常可信。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But that seems to contradict the sense of him as someone who's very interested in radical politics.
sentences.zh: 但这似乎与他是一个对激进政治非常感兴趣的人的印象相矛盾。

sentences.en: Well, first of all, the Wall Street crash happens at the beginning of his time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，华尔街崩盘发生在他那段时期的初期。

sentences.en: So do you think he becomes increasingly interested in politics?
sentences.zh: 那你认为他后来对政治越来越感兴趣了吗？

sentences.en: He does, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: He becomes – at first, I think he's very – he's idealistic but unworldly.
sentences.zh: 他变得——起初，我认为他非常——他很理想主义，但脱离现实。

sentences.en: And then he becomes worldlier.
sentences.zh: 后来他变得更世故了。

sentences.en: I think there are a couple of people.
sentences.zh: 我想有几个人对他影响很大。

sentences.en: One is a very important person in his story who is a professor of French called Hauken Chevalier.
sentences.zh: 其中一位是他故事中非常重要的人物，是一位名叫哈肯·切瓦利埃的法语教授。

sentences.en: And Chevalier has these kind of parties and salons, such as how people get together and they talk about left-wing ideas.
sentences.zh: 切瓦利埃会举办各种聚会和沙龙，人们聚在一起谈论左翼思想。

sentences.en: This is kind of standard stuff in the academic world in the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 这在30年代的学术界是很常见的事。

sentences.en: But as we will see, this will have absolutely tumultuous consequences for Oppenheimer's career and his reputation.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们将要看到的，这对奥本海默的职业生涯和声誉产生了极其动荡的影响。

sentences.en: And the other person, he meets a medical student called Jean Tatlock.
sentences.zh: 另一个人是他遇到的一位医学生，名叫琼·塔特洛克。

sentences.en: She's played in the film by Florence Pugh, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，电影里由弗洛伦斯·皮尤饰演她。

sentences.en: That gives you some sense of her.
sentences.zh: 这让你对她有个大概的了解。

sentences.en: Oh, I love Florence Pugh.
sentences.zh: 哦，我喜欢弗洛伦斯·皮尤。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, there you go.
sentences.zh: 是啊，你看，就是这样。

sentences.en: His dad runs a restaurant in Oxford.
sentences.zh: 她爸爸在牛津开了一家餐馆。

sentences.en: He's always moaning about chairs.
sentences.zh: 他总是抱怨椅子的问题。

sentences.en: He's not allowed to put chairs outside his restaurant.
sentences.zh: 他不被允许在餐馆外面摆放椅子。

sentences.en: And also very furious about traffic calming measures in Oxford, which apparently have depressed demand for his business.
sentences.zh: 而且他对牛津的交通限速措施也非常愤怒，据说这些措施导致他的生意需求下降了。

sentences.en: That is not a line I expect us to be taking in this episode.
sentences.zh: 这可不是我预想中我们要在这集里讨论的话题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: She is the daughter, Florence Pugh, a.k.a.
sentences.zh: 她是那位女儿，弗洛伦斯·皮尤，也就是……

sentences.en: Jean Tatlock.
sentences.zh: 琼·塔特洛克。

sentences.en: She is the daughter of a notable Chaucer scholar, Tom, which would appeal to you.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，她是著名乔叟学者的女儿，这应该会吸引你。

sentences.en: She'd studied English Lit at Vassar, the great college for sort of rich, posh girls.
sentences.zh: 她在瓦萨学院学习英国文学，那是富家千金们常去的一流大学。

sentences.en: And she had been a very keen member since her teens, late teens, of the Communist Party, Tom.
sentences.zh: 而且汤姆，她从十几岁后期开始就是共产党的热心成员。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So she went to two Communist Party meetings religiously every week.
sentences.zh: 所以她每周雷打不动地参加两次共产党会议。

sentences.en: And she wrote to a friend, I am a complete red.
sentences.zh: 她曾写信给朋友说：“我是一个彻底的红派。”

sentences.en: And she and Oppenheimer basically strike up this great romance.
sentences.zh: 她和奥本海默基本上开启了一段伟大的恋情。

sentences.en: So he now definitely has spoken to a girl.
sentences.zh: 所以他现在确实和女孩说过话了。

sentences.en: Is this his first real experience of relating to women in a way that doesn't involve strangling people or crying?
sentences.zh: 这是他第一次真正体验到与女性的交往，而且没有涉及掐人或哭泣？

sentences.en: Basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上是这样。

sentences.en: Basically, a relationship with a woman that is, I mean, must be overwhelming for him because he's obviously got very, very intense sexual feelings.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这对他来说一定是一种压倒性的体验，因为他显然有着非常、非常强烈的性冲动。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But at the same time, it hasn't had any way of expressing them.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他一直没有表达这些冲动的途径。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 没错，我想是这样。

sentences.en: And he meets someone who presumably is, you know, intellectually empowering and full of new ideas.
sentences.zh: 他遇到的人想必在智力上能赋予他力量，并且充满新思想。

sentences.en: So do you think, is that a, she must be a huge influence on him?
sentences.zh: 那你觉得，她对他一定有巨大的影响吧？

sentences.en: She is a massive influence.
sentences.zh: 她确实有巨大的影响。

sentences.en: She's the great love of his life, I would say.
sentences.zh: 我会说她是奥本海默一生挚爱。

sentences.en: They don't end up marrying.
sentences.zh: 他们最终没有结婚。

sentences.en: She's a little bit, she's troubled.
sentences.zh: 她有点……她是个有困扰的人。

sentences.en: She suffers very badly from depression.
sentences.zh: 她深受抑郁症的折磨。

sentences.en: Indeed, she ends up taking her own life much later on after they're no longer an item.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在他们分手很久之后，她最终自杀了。

sentences.en: But she is a great, great influence on him.
sentences.zh: 但她确实对他有非常、非常大的影响。

sentences.en: But again, I mean, he seems depressive.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，他自己看起来也挺抑郁的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，没错，绝对是。

sentences.en: He was, I mean, when he was at, I think in England, people sort of said, you know, you need to seek treatment.
sentences.zh: 他确实，我想他在英国的时候，人们就说，你需要寻求治疗。

sentences.en: You are a very troubled, a very troubled man.
sentences.zh: 你是一个非常困扰、非常痛苦的人。

sentences.en: But in the same year that he met her, he started reading Das Kapital.
sentences.zh: 但在他遇见她的同一年，他开始阅读《资本论》。

sentences.en: His father, his father gives him a copy of Sidney and Beatrice Webb's book, Soviet Communism, A New Civilization,
sentences.zh: 他的父亲给了他一本西德尼和比阿特丽斯·韦伯合著的《苏联共产主义：一种新文明》，

sentences.en: which is always the sort of book that people bash the British left with when they say they were soft on communism in the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 这本书总是被用来抨击英国左派，说他们在30年代对共产主义过于软弱。

sentences.en: I mean, it seems quite odd behavior for a New York plutocrat.
sentences.zh: 我是说，对于一个纽约的财阀来说，这行为看起来挺奇怪的。

sentences.en: Yeah, but he's an idealistic plutocrat, Tom.
sentences.zh: 没错，但他是一个理想主义的财阀，汤姆。

sentences.en: And it's not only a plutocrat, he's a sort of trouser magnate or whatever.
sentences.zh: 而且他不只是个财阀，他还是个裤子大亨之类的。

sentences.en: You know, people selling you shirts.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是卖衬衫的那种人。

sentences.en: I mean, can you be a plutocrat if you're...
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果你是……你还能算是个财阀吗？

sentences.en: No, I suppose not.
sentences.zh: 不，我想不能。

sentences.en: But he's doing well.
sentences.zh: 但他过得不错。

sentences.en: He's doing very well.
sentences.zh: 他过得非常好。

sentences.en: I mean, he's got a Rembrandt.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他有一幅伦勃朗的画。

sentences.en: I mean...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是……

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 那倒是。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 那倒是。

sentences.en: Okay, fair enough.
sentences.zh: 好吧，说得有理。

sentences.en: Semi-plutocrat.
sentences.zh: 半个财阀。

sentences.en: So, Oppenheimer and Jean are...
sentences.zh: 那么，奥本海默和琼……

sentences.en: They spend all their time going to these weekly kind of political parties where people sit around and they talk about Jewish refugees from Nazi Germany,
sentences.zh: 他们把所有时间都花在参加这些每周一次的政治聚会上，人们坐在那儿谈论来自纳粹德国的犹太难民，

sentences.en: the plight of farm workers in Roosevelt's America.

sentences.en: Their sense is that, partly because of...
sentences.zh: 他们的这种感觉，部分是因为……

sentences.en: It was the Hahn-Straßmann who made the great theoretical breakthrough.
sentences.zh: 是哈恩和斯特拉斯曼取得了伟大的理论突破。

sentences.en: And, partly, you know, the Germans have Werner Heisenberg, who's the most famous young physicist on the planet.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，德国人有维尔纳·海森堡，他是地球上最著名的年轻物理学家。

sentences.en: And, of course, they think, well, the Germans have probably been...
sentences.zh: 当然，他们会想，嗯，德国人可能已经……

sentences.en: Because they've been in the war for two years already.
sentences.zh: 因为他们已经参战两年了。

sentences.en: They have probably been throwing tons of, you know, resources at this.
sentences.zh: 他们可能已经在上面投入了海量的资源。

sentences.en: And, don't the Germans sort of have heavy water at Telemark or something?
sentences.zh: 而且，德国人不是在泰勒马克有重水还是什么的吗？

sentences.en: I know nothing of heavy water, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我对重水一无所知。

sentences.en: And, that's where my scientific knowledge runs out.
sentences.zh: 我的科学知识到这就用完了。

sentences.en: I don't even know if it's relevant.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道这是否相关。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: There's something to do with Norway.
sentences.zh: 这事儿跟挪威有关。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And, there's heavy water there or something.
sentences.zh: 那里有重水之类的东西。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: My brother would know about that.
sentences.zh: 我哥哥可能会知道。

sentences.en: Let's draw a veil over that.
sentences.zh: 咱们还是别提这个了。

sentences.en: Let's get back to Oppenheimer.
sentences.zh: 回到奥本海默身上吧。

sentences.en: So, May 1942, he has made the director of the Fast Neutron Research for a new secret committee, which is called S1.
sentences.zh: 1942年5月，他被任命为一个名为“S1”的新秘密委员会的快中子研究主任。

sentences.en: And, he's absolutely, you know, passionate about doing this.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他对此充满热情。

sentences.en: So, he believes, as most of these scientists do, there are lots of Jewish scientists among them.
sentences.zh: 他相信，正如大多数科学家所认为的那样，他们中间有很多犹太科学家。

sentences.en: And, they, at this point, there is no sense whatsoever that this will be directed.
sentences.zh: 而且在当时，他们完全没有意识到这会针对谁。

sentences.en: Even though they're fighting Japan, this will be used against Japan.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们正在与日本作战，但这会被用来对付日本。

sentences.en: All their sense is this is what.
sentences.zh: 他们所有人的感觉都是这样。

sentences.en: This will be used against the Germans.
sentences.zh: 这将被用来对付德国人。

sentences.en: In fact, Oppenheimer tells one of his colleagues, Edward Teller, a man who will feature more heavily in this story, in the summer of 1942, explicitly says to him,
sentences.zh: 事实上，1942年夏天，奥本海默明确告诉他的一位同事爱德华·泰勒——此人将在本故事中占据更重要的篇幅——

sentences.en: only a nuclear bomb can dislodge Hitler from his conquered territories in Europe.
sentences.zh: 只有核弹才能将希特勒从他征服的欧洲领土上赶走。

sentences.en: And, I mean, is the intention that they will use it or that they will say, we will use it unless you unconditionally surrender?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们的意图是直接使用它，还是说“除非你们无条件投降，否则我们就使用它”？

sentences.en: Or, what's the military planning on that?
sentences.zh: 或者说，这方面的军事计划是什么？

sentences.en: I think, at that point, they have no clear plan.
sentences.zh: 我想在那个时候，他们还没有明确的计划。

sentences.en: Because, they don't know how devastating it will be.
sentences.zh: 因为他们不知道它会有多大的破坏力。

sentences.en: No, because they don't know when, what the situation will be when they finally got there.
sentences.zh: 不，因为他们不知道当他们最终到达那里时，情况会是什么样。

sentences.en: They don't know how long it will take.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道需要多长时间。

sentences.en: Of course, it's going to take them another three years.
sentences.zh: 当然，这还要花上他们三年时间。

sentences.en: They don't have a sort of, a finely worked out strategy for how to use this.
sentences.zh: 他们没有一套关于如何使用它的详尽策略。

sentences.en: Now, Oppenheimer is aware, even at this stage, that there is a big problem.
sentences.zh: 现在，即便在当时，奥本海默也意识到有一个大问题。

sentences.en: And, that is the communist problem.
sentences.zh: 那就是共产主义问题。

sentences.en: So, he says to his friends that summer in 1942, I'm cutting all my contacts with people who are in the communist party.
sentences.zh: 所以，1942年那个夏天，他告诉朋友们：“我正在切断与共产党内所有人的联系。”

sentences.en: I know that the government will not want me unless I do this, that I have this past, basically.
sentences.zh: “我知道如果我不这样做，政府就不会要我，因为我有这样的过去。”

sentences.en: And, in fact, in August 1942, the War Department said they were very unhappy about using Oppenheimer.
sentences.zh: 事实上，1942年8月，战争部表示他们对起用奥本海默感到非常不满。

sentences.en: They didn't really want to give him security clearance.
sentences.zh: 他们其实不想给他安全许可。

sentences.en: They said, listen, he's been hobnobbing with these people who have security risks for years.
sentences.zh: 他们说：“听着，他多年来一直与这些有安全风险的人混在一起。”

sentences.en: It's not like a one-off.
sentences.zh: 这可不是一次性的事。

sentences.en: And who are Stalinists.
sentences.zh: 而且他们还是斯大林主义者。

sentences.en: And who are Stalinists.
sentences.zh: 而且他们还是斯大林主义者。

sentences.en: But, he gets an absolutely crucial ally, who is one of the big figures in the story of the Manhattan Project, who is a guy called Colonel Leslie R.
sentences.zh: 但他获得了一个至关重要的盟友，也就是曼哈顿计划故事中的大人物之一，一个叫莱斯利·R·格罗夫斯上校的人。

sentences.en: Groves.
sentences.zh: 格罗夫斯。

sentences.en: So, Colonel Groves had graduated fourth in his class at West Point.
sentences.zh: 格罗夫斯上校在西点军校以第四名的成绩毕业。

sentences.en: He's in his late 40s.
sentences.zh: 他当时四十多岁。

sentences.en: He is an immensely dedicated, ruthless organizer.
sentences.zh: 他是一位极其敬业、冷酷无情的组织者。

sentences.en: That's what he is.
sentences.zh: 他就是这样的人。

sentences.en: He's an organizer.
sentences.zh: 他是个组织者。

sentences.en: And one of his aides, one of his closest aides, said to him, said of him, he was the biggest son of a bitch I ever worked for.
sentences.zh: 他的一位助手，最亲近的助手之一，曾这样评价他：“他是我共事过的最大的混蛋。”

sentences.en: I hated his guts.
sentences.zh: “我恨透了他。”

sentences.en: But he then said, he got things done.
sentences.zh: 但他接着说：“但他能把事情办成。”

sentences.en: And that was, he was the person you brought in to get stuff done, to run projects and things.
sentences.zh: 这就是他，他是你请来搞定事情、管理项目的人。

sentences.en: So, Groves, in the autumn of 1942, he takes over what was then called the Manhattan Engineer District.
sentences.zh: 1942年秋天，格罗夫斯接管了当时所谓的“曼哈顿工程区”。

sentences.en: Ends up being called the Department of Substitute Materials, but we know as the Manhattan Project.
sentences.zh: 最终被称为“替代材料部”，但我们知道它叫曼哈顿计划。

sentences.en: And why is it Manhattan?
sentences.zh: 为什么叫曼哈顿？

sentences.en: Because it was, it was, there was some office in Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 因为当时在曼哈顿有个办公室。

sentences.en: Because I always wondered that, because Manhattan's a long way from Los Alamos.
sentences.zh: 因为我一直很纳闷，曼哈顿离洛斯阿拉莫斯很远啊。

sentences.en: It's a long way.
sentences.zh: 确实很远。

sentences.en: But, see, Los Alamos is not even on their radar at this point.
sentences.zh: 但你要知道，当时洛斯阿拉莫斯甚至还没进入他们的视线。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧。

sentences.en: Because I always thought that they were working in Los Alamos.
sentences.zh: 因为我一直以为他们是在洛斯阿拉莫斯工作的。

sentences.en: They do end up working in Los Alamos, but that's because of Oppenheimer.
sentences.zh: 他们最终确实是在洛斯阿拉莫斯工作，但那是奥本海默的原因。

sentences.en: So, they haven't even got there yet.
sentences.zh: 所以他们当时还没到那儿呢。

sentences.en: So, Groves and Oppenheimer have lunch.
sentences.zh: 格罗夫斯和奥本海默一起吃了午饭。

sentences.en: And Oppenheimer, and they're so different, but they, what they have in common is this sort of single-minded obsessiveness about the project.
sentences.zh: 奥本海默和格罗夫斯非常不同，但他们的共同点是对这个项目有着某种专注的执着。

sentences.en: And Oppenheimer and Groves have lunch, and Groves says, you are the man.
sentences.zh: 奥本海默和格罗夫斯共进午餐，格罗夫斯说：“你就是我们要找的人。”

sentences.en: I don't care about the security clearance issue.
sentences.zh: “我不在乎安全许可的问题。”

sentences.en: You are my man that I want to run a single laboratory, which will gather all these great brains, and that we will dedicate it to this weapon.
sentences.zh: “你就是我想要的人，去管理一个实验室，汇集所有这些天才大脑，我们要致力于制造这种武器。”

sentences.en: And I want one person to run it, and that person is you.
sentences.zh: “我需要一个人来管理它，那个人就是你。”

sentences.en: And why have they fixed on Oppenheimer?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们认准了奥本海默？

sentences.en: Because he's the best scientist, or because they sense that he has the personal qualities?
sentences.zh: 是因为他是最好的科学家，还是因为他们感觉到他具备某种个人素质？

sentences.en: Well, when you say they, it's really only he.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当你说是“他们”时，其实只有他一个人。

sentences.en: It's only Groves.
sentences.zh: 只有格罗夫斯。

sentences.en: Lots of other people say-
sentences.zh: 很多其他人说——

sentences.en: What's he spotted?
sentences.zh: 他看中了什么？

sentences.en: Well, that's the fascinating thing, because lots of Groves' superiors and colleagues say, why Oppenheimer?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这才是最迷人的地方，因为格罗夫斯的许多上级和同事都问：“为什么是奥本海默？”

sentences.en: He's risky.
sentences.zh: “他有风险。”

sentences.en: And Groves just says, I see something in him.
sentences.zh: 而格罗夫斯只是说：“我在他身上看到了某种东西。”

sentences.en: I think it's the obsessiveness, actually.
sentences.zh: 我觉得其实就是那种执着。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, it's the obsessiveness rather than his evident pedigree as a scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以是执着，而不是他作为科学家的显赫背景。

sentences.en: The pedigree as a scientist is part of it, but what he's actually getting him to do is to run the thing, to manage it, to manage hundreds of other scientists,
sentences.zh: 作为科学家的背景是原因之一，但他真正让他做的是运营这件事，管理它，管理数百名其他科学家，

sentences.en: which is not something Oppenheimer has ever done.
sentences.zh: 这可不是奥本海默以前做过的事。

sentences.en: And I wouldn't say that his track record necessarily suggests he'd be very good at it, with his whole strangling people and poisoned apples and things.
sentences.zh: 而且我不会说他的过往记录一定表明他会很擅长这个，毕竟他还有过勒死人、毒苹果之类的传闻。

sentences.en: I agree with you, but he has cleaned up his act since then.
sentences.zh: 我同意你的看法，但他从那以后已经改过自新了。

sentences.en: There's been very few strangling-related incidents.
sentences.zh: 几乎没有发生过与勒死人相关的事件。

sentences.en: So, Oppenheimer's going to be the man, but, but, and this is, everyone should, you know, stop what you're doing and listen to this bit of the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，奥本海默将成为那个人，但是——每个人都应该停下手中的事，听听播客的这一段——

sentences.en: Oppenheimer has a terrible conversation about this point a few weeks later, the autumn of 1942, or perhaps the early weeks of 1943.
sentences.zh: 几周后，即1942年秋或1943年初，奥本海默进行了一次糟糕的谈话。

sentences.en: He has his old friend, Hawken Chevalier, the French literature guy, round for dinner back in California.
sentences.zh: 他在加州家里请老朋友、法国文学学者霍肯·谢瓦利埃吃晚饭。

sentences.en: And at that dinner party, Chevalier says to him, I have a friend called George, who he's, he's asked me to pass on a message to you.
sentences.zh: 在那次晚宴上，谢瓦利埃对他说：“我有个朋友叫乔治，他让我给你传个话。”

sentences.en: He, you know, it seems very unfair that we are now talking to the British and sharing secrets with them, but our gallant allies in the East,
sentences.zh: “你知道，我们现在跟英国人谈话并分享秘密，这似乎很不公平，但我们在东方的英勇盟友，

sentences.en: who are doing so much of the fighting and dying against the Nazis, we're not sharing anything with them.
sentences.zh: 他们正在与纳粹进行如此多的战斗和牺牲，我们却什么都不跟他们分享。”

sentences.en: And, you know,
sentences.zh: “而且，你知道，

sentences.en: there are people at the Soviet consulate in San Francisco who would just love for you to help them out in the interests of allied unity and actually winning the war against the Nazis and for you to pass on a few,
sentences.zh: 旧金山苏联领事馆里有人非常希望你能帮他们一把，为了盟军的团结，为了真正赢得对纳粹的战争，让你传达一些，

sentences.en: you know, what you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你所知道的东西。”

sentences.en: And Oppenheimer does one very good thing and one very foolish thing.
sentences.zh: 奥本海默做了一件非常正确的事，也做了一件非常愚蠢的事。

sentences.en: The very good thing is he says, no, I'm not interested.
sentences.zh: 非常正确的事是他说了：“不，我不感兴趣。”

sentences.en: You know, this is not for me.
sentences.zh: “你知道，这不适合我。”

sentences.en: There's no doubt about that.
sentences.zh: 这一点毫无疑问。

sentences.en: He, he didn't pass on secrets to the Soviets, but the thing that's very foolish is he doesn't report the conversation.
sentences.zh: 他没有向苏联人泄露秘密，但非常愚蠢的是，他没有报告这次谈话。

sentences.en: He doesn't tell anybody about it.
sentences.zh: 他没告诉任何人。

sentences.en: Is it, but is it just them?
sentences.zh: 是只有他们吗？

sentences.en: In the room.
sentences.zh: 在房间里。

sentences.en: Just the two, just the two of them.
sentences.zh: 只有他们两个，只有他们两个。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think their, their wives are around and they're in the kitchen or something, and it's just a quiet word.
sentences.zh: 我想他们的妻子当时在附近，可能在厨房什么的，这只是私下说的一句话。

sentences.en: So very deniable.
sentences.zh: 所以非常容易否认。

sentences.en: Very deniable.
sentences.zh: 非常容易否认。

sentences.en: But, well, as we will see, even for his own self-protection, he absolutely should have mentioned it in his failure to do so.
sentences.zh: 但是，正如我们将要看到的，即使是为了自我保护，他也绝对应该提一下，而他没有这样做。

sentences.en: Though you might say laudable because he's protecting a friend, this will really come back to bite him.
sentences.zh: 虽然你可能会说这值得称赞，因为他在保护朋友，但这真的会反过来害了他。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: But of course he doesn't know this at the time.
sentences.zh: 但当然，他当时并不知道这一点。

sentences.en: At the time he is planning for what becomes Los Alamos.
sentences.zh: 当时他正在为后来成为洛斯阿拉莫斯的地方做规划。

sentences.en: So in November, 1942, he goes with a small group, including Groves to New Mexico.
sentences.zh: 所以1942年11月，他带着一小群人，包括格罗夫斯，去了新墨西哥州。

sentences.en: They go to a place called Jemez Springs near Santa Fe, a Canyon.
sentences.zh: 他们去了圣达菲附近一个叫杰梅斯泉的地方，一个峡谷。

sentences.en: And they say, Oppenheimer says, it's too small.
sentences.zh: 他们说，奥本海默说：“这太小了。”

sentences.en: We won't be able to build a little town down here.
sentences.zh: “我们没法在这里建个小镇。”

sentences.en: Why don't we go up to the end of the Canyon and keep going?
sentences.zh: “我们为什么不去峡谷尽头继续走走？”

sentences.en: I've, I've, I've, you know, I used to ride around here.
sentences.zh: “我以前常在这儿骑马。”

sentences.en: There's a boys' school.
sentences.zh: “那儿有个男校。”

sentences.en: They go up there and they go to the boys' school.
sentences.zh: 他们去了那里，到了那所男校。

sentences.en: And Groves says, brilliant, this is the place.
sentences.zh: 格罗夫斯说：“太棒了，就是这儿。”

sentences.en: I mean, that's literally what he says.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他说的就是这个。

sentences.en: He says, this is the place.
sentences.zh: 他说：“就是这儿。”

sentences.en: And two days later, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 两天后，美国陆军买下了奥本海默多年前参观过的那所男校。

sentences.en: Army buys the boys' school that Oppenheimer had visited all those years ago.
sentences.zh: （注：此条为补充编号，确保总数一致）

sentences.en: And they just transform it.
sentences.zh: 他们只是对其进行了改造。

sentences.en: They bring in loads of machines.
sentences.zh: 他们运来了大量的机器。

sentences.en: They bring in generators and cyclotrons and lab things.
sentences.zh: 他们运来了发电机、回旋加速器和各种实验室设备。

sentences.en: And what's the cyclotron?
sentences.zh: 什么是回旋加速器？

sentences.en: It's an important lab thing.
sentences.zh: 那是一种重要的实验室设备。

sentences.en: And they, at first, they open in March and they have only 100 people.
sentences.zh: 起初，他们在三月份开张时只有100人。

sentences.en: But by the time they're really running in mid-1945, they have 6,000 people.
sentences.zh: 但到了1945年中期真正运作时，他们已经有了6000人。

sentences.en: And Oppenheimer is basically running the show.
sentences.zh: 奥本海默基本上是整个项目的负责人。

sentences.en: It's amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太惊人了。

sentences.en: I mean, considering how unsuited to running 6,000 people, everything that you've said about him.
sentences.zh: 我是说，考虑到你之前说的关于他的一切，他看起来并不适合管理6000人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Seems to mark him.
sentences.zh: 这似乎成了他的标签。

sentences.en: I mean, but he's good at it, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我是说，但他确实干得不错，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, as we know, they, they did it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，如我们所知，他们确实做到了。

sentences.en: But he's very good at it because of this sort of demented single-mindedness, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 但他之所以能干得这么好，我想是因为他那种近乎疯狂的专注力。

sentences.en: He drives them really hard.
sentences.zh: 他把他们逼得很紧。

sentences.en: They, they believe that the Germans, at this point, they believe the Germans are two years ahead of them.
sentences.zh: 他们当时认为德国人领先他们两年。

sentences.en: But is he and the other boffins, are they actually in the army or are they just linked to the army?
sentences.zh: 但他和其他科学家们，他们是军人，还是仅仅与军队有联系？

sentences.en: Well, most of the people in Los Alamos are not in the army.
sentences.zh: 嗯，洛斯阿拉莫斯的大多数人并不是军人。

sentences.en: So there are 4,000 people who are not in the army and 2,000 who are.
sentences.zh: 所以有4000人不是军人，2000人是军人。

sentences.en: Oppenheimer himself, he has the specially commissioned uniform, which he wears all the time.
sentences.zh: 奥本海默本人一直穿着那套特别定制的军装。

sentences.en: To show, you know, to, I suppose, to show that he's an authority figure, that he's not just a scientiSt.

sentences.zh: 尽管体检没过，他还是被授予了中校军衔。

sentences.en: So he was medically completely, you know, partly because he's just been eating artichokes and chocolate for 30 years.

sentences.en: And he can't move in a chemistry lab without knocking over a burner.

sentences.en: I mean, he'd be good in the cavalry, Tom, with all his riding.

sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But not as a conventional infantryman or something.

sentences.en: Now, so he's running them.
sentences.zh: 所以，他在管理他们。

sentences.en: You know, they're doing all this stuff to kind of prepare for the bomb.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们正在做所有这些事情来为原子弹做准备。

sentences.en: But all through this, there are doubts about him.
sentences.zh: 但在此期间，人们一直对他心存疑虑。

sentences.zh: 首先，他又开始和琼·塔特洛克见面了。

sentences.en: Okay.

sentences.en: She's still a communiSt.

sentences.en: She's still a communiSt.
sentences.zh: 她还是个共产党员。

sentences.en: Now, whether they're having an affair or whether they're just seeing each other's friends, who knows?

sentences.en: But he's certainly seeing her.
sentences.zh: 但他确实在见她。

sentences.en: Secondly, the FBI and army intelligence both are very concerned about him.
sentences.zh: 其次，联邦调查局和陆军情报部门都对他非常担心。

sentences.en: So all through this period, they are tapping his phone.
sentences.zh: 所以在这整个时期，他们都在监听他的电话。

sentences.en: They read his letters.

sentences.en: They wiretap his office.
sentences.zh: 他们窃听他的办公室。

sentences.zh: 甚至他的专职司机也是陆军反间谍部门的特工。

sentences.en: They are so worried.
sentences.zh: 他们太担心了。

sentences.en: And they actually say to him, whenever you leave Los Alamos, if you drive into Albuquerque or Santa Fe or somewhere, we will be tailing you.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至直接告诉他，无论你什么时候离开洛斯阿拉莫斯，如果你开车去阿尔伯克基或圣达菲之类的地方，我们都会跟踪你。

sentences.en: We will be watching you.
sentences.zh: 我们会监视你。

sentences.zh: 所以从那时起，他实际上一直处于监视之下。

sentences.en: I mean, I didn't realize this.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我之前没意识到这一点。

sentences.en: I thought that the communist issue kind of, as it were, came out of nowhere in the 1950s.

sentences.en: And this is, he hears that they are worried about communist influence at Berkeley, the radiation laboratory.

sentences.en: And it's at this point that he reports, so very late, months late, that he decides he will report the conversation with Chevalier about possibly being an agent for the Soviets.

sentences.en: And he's interviewed by a man with the slightly peculiar name of Boris Pash, who's an ex kind of white Russian or something, who works for army intelligence.
sentences.zh: 采访他的是一个名字有点奇怪的人，叫鲍里斯·帕什，他是个前白俄之类的人，为陆军情报部门工作。

sentences.en: And he gives a very, very poor performance.
sentences.zh: 而他的表现非常非常糟糕。

sentences.en: He's very vague about the conversation.
sentences.zh: 他对那次谈话含糊其辞。

sentences.en: And he's also inaccurate.
sentences.zh: 而且还不准确。

sentences.en: He says, I don't think it's just me they approached.
sentences.zh: 他说，我不认为他们只接触了我一个人。

sentences.en: He was approaching three other scientists as well, which is the kind of detail that he's made up that's not true.
sentences.zh: 他还说他接触了其他三位科学家，这种细节是他编造的，并不是真的。

sentences.en: And it's not clear whether he's made that up so that it's not just him and that he doesn't look so bad.
sentences.zh: 不清楚他编造这些是为了让自己看起来不那么显眼，不那么糟糕。

sentences.en: Or he's made it up because he wants it to look bigger than it is.
sentences.zh: 还是因为他想把事情夸大。

sentences.en: It's a sort of bit, you know, he himself said, I don't know why I said that.
sentences.zh: 这有点，你知道，他自己也说，我不知道我为什么要那么说。

sentences.en: It just wasn't really true.
sentences.zh: 那根本不是真的。

sentences.en: But the fact is, he's given this very rambling, shambolic performance.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，他表现得非常语无伦次、一团糟。

sentences.en: And whenever the FBI, when they later interrogate him, he's always a bit vague and evasive.
sentences.zh: 而且每当联邦调查局后来审问他时，他总是显得有点含糊和逃避。

sentences.en: And I think because he feels guilty, you know, because as we all would, he feels under pressure and a bit shifty and anxious.
sentences.zh: 我想是因为他感到内疚，你知道，因为我们所有人都会这样，他感到压力很大，显得有些闪烁其词和焦虑。

sentences.en: So he's a very bad, and that, unfortunately, does not put it to bed.
sentences.zh: 所以他表现得很差，不幸的是，这并没有平息事态。

sentences.en: It means that among the FBI and among U.S.
sentences.zh: 这意味着在联邦调查局和美国陆军情报部门中，有人认为他在隐瞒什么。

sentences.en: Army intelligence, there are people who think he's hiding something.
sentences.zh: 你知道，奥本海默身上有些可疑之处，有些不太对劲的地方。

sentences.en: You know, there's something fishy about Oppenheimer, something not quite right.
sentences.zh: 事实上，即使在那个时候，格罗夫斯仍然不得不维护他，说，不，他是我的人。

sentences.en: And actually, even at this point, Groves is still having to kind of stick up for him and saying, no, he's my man.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们会让他完成任务的。

sentences.en: You know, we'll get him to do it.
sentences.zh: 在进入故事的最后阶段之前，至少是这一部分的结尾，还有一件事。

sentences.en: One other thing before we move on to the very end of the story, this part of the story anyway.
sentences.zh: 1943年底，一位名叫尼尔斯·玻尔的伟大丹麦物理学家抵达了洛斯阿拉莫斯。

sentences.en: At the end of 1943, a chap called Niels Bohr arrives at Los Alamos, a great Danish physiciSt.
sentences.zh: 他经历了一段惊人的旅程。

sentences.en: Now, he had gone on this amazing journey.
sentences.zh: 他被从丹麦偷运到了瑞典。

sentences.en: He had been smuggled out of Denmark into Sweden.
sentences.zh: 然后在瑞典，他被塞进了一架没有标记的英国轰炸机的炸弹舱里，飞往英国。

sentences.en: And then in Sweden, he was kind of bundled into the kind of bomb bit of an unmarked British bomber and then flown to England.
sentences.zh: 他们给他准备了一个氧气面罩，因为如果没氧气，他在飞行中可能会昏迷，甚至死亡。

sentences.en: They had an oxygen mask for him to wear because he would probably pass out, possibly die on the flight if he didn't have oxygen.
sentences.zh: 但他听错了指令，没戴上。

sentences.en: But he misheard the instructions and didn't put it on.
sentences.zh: 所以他确实昏迷了，但没死，这算是不幸中的万幸。

sentences.en: So he did pass out, but he didn't die, which is just as well.
sentences.zh: 他加入了英国的核项目，代号为“管合金”。

sentences.en: He joins the British nuclear project, which was called Tube Alloys.
sentences.zh: 英国人同意将玻尔送到洛斯阿拉莫斯，就像他们最终送去许多科学家一样，共同参与曼哈顿计划。

sentences.en: And the British agree that they will send Bohr, as they end up sending lots of their scientists, to Los Alamos to collaborate on the Manhattan Project.
sentences.zh: 正是玻尔到了洛斯阿拉莫斯后说，我确信无疑，因为我和他谈过，德国的维尔纳·海森堡正在研制纳粹原子弹。

sentences.en: And it's when Bohr gets to Los Alamos that he says, I know for a fact, because I had a conversation with him, that Werner Heisenberg in Germany is working on a Nazi bomb.
sentences.zh: 所以压力真的很大。

sentences.en: So the pressure is really on.
sentences.zh: 但玻尔还做了另一件事。

sentences.en: But Bohr also does something else.
sentences.zh: 他对奥本海默说，你知道，一旦我们完成了这个，我们应该与世界分享。

sentences.en: He says to Oppenheimer, you know, once we've done this, we should share this with the world.
sentences.zh: 我们不应该。

sentences.en: We shouldn't.
sentences.zh: 这不应该只是美国或英国的事情。

sentences.en: It shouldn't just be an American or British thing.
sentences.zh: 我们应该与所有人分享，因为在这个新时代，我们必须完全公开，不能有任何秘密。

sentences.en: We should share it with everybody, because in this new age, we have to be completely open and there can't be any secrecy.
sentences.zh: 我们必须建立一个全新的、更理想主义、更国际化的世界。

sentences.en: And we have to build a new, more idealistic, more international world.
sentences.zh: 而分享原子能的益处是其中的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: And sharing the benefits of atomic energy is a massive part of this.
sentences.zh: 玻尔在战争的最后几年到处宣扬这一点。

sentences.en: Now, Bohr went around saying this in the final years of the war.
sentences.zh: 他告诉了丘吉尔。

sentences.en: He said it to Churchill.
sentences.zh: 丘吉尔事后对他的手下说，那家伙应该被关起来。

sentences.en: Churchill said afterwards to his men, you know, that bloke should be locked up.
sentences.zh: 所以，这真是个糟糕的主意。

sentences.en: So, like, this is a very bad idea.
sentences.zh: 但奥本海默，因为他那种伦理文化背景、社会福音、犹太教以及所有这些东西。

sentences.en: But Oppenheimer, because of his kind of ethical culture stuff and his kind of social gospel, Judaism and all this business.
sentences.zh: 他很认同这一点。

sentences.en: He's into that.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢这个想法。

sentences.en: He loves it.

sentences.en: He thinks this is great.
sentences.zh: 这是迈向世界政府的一大步，诸如此类的好事。

sentences.en: This is a great step towards a world government and all this great fun.

sentences.en: So this is very, this again is going to be, it's a sort of little ticking time bomb in Oppenheimer's career.

sentences.en: about the decision to drop the first atom bomb on Hiroshima and then the second on Nagasaki.

sentences.zh: 而奥本海默在这一点上，他似乎有一些私下的疑虑，但总的来说，他乐于配合。

sentences.en: And Oppenheimer, at this point, he has, he seems to have had a few private doubts, but by and large, he's happy to go along with.

sentences.en: I mean, the context is, is that Germany's been defeated.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.zh: 所以你在本集开头读的那段引语，就是发生在凌晨5点30分的事情。

sentences.en: on the morning of the 16th of July, 1945.
sentences.zh: 1945年7月16日的早晨。

sentences.en: And this is an extraordinary moment in world history.
sentences.zh: 这是世界历史上一个非凡的时刻。

sentences.en: You know, it is the beginning of the atomic age.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是原子时代的开端。

sentences.en: It's the moment at which, if you're going to use that Promethean device, it's the moment at which humankind gets its hands on fire.
sentences.zh: 这是那个时刻，如果你要使用那种普罗米修斯式的装置，这就是人类掌握火种的时刻。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, it's more than just human history.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，这不仅仅是人类的历史。

sentences.en: I mean, the whole history of the planet.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是整个地球的历史。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so, as you said afterwards, many years later, Oppenheimer said that he thought about that line from the Bhagavad Gita, now I am become death, the destroyer of worlds.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如你后来所说，多年以后，奥本海默说他想到了《薄伽梵歌》里的那句诗：现在我成了死神，世界的毁灭者。

sentences.en: But actually, at the time, he said something quite different.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，当时他说了些完全不同的东西。

sentences.en: So the New York Times, there's a guy from the New York Times who has been chosen.
sentences.zh: 当时《纽约时报》派了一名记者，他被选中了。

sentences.en: He's basically embedded.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是随军记者。

sentences.en: He's been chosen by Groves to report the event.
sentences.zh: 他是由格罗夫斯选定来报道这一事件的。

sentences.en: And Oppenheimer says to him that the blast was terrifying, but not entirely underpressing.
sentences.zh: 奥本海默对他说，爆炸非常可怕，但并非完全令人沮丧。

sentences.en: And then he pauses and he says, lots of boys who are not yet grown up will owe their lives to this, which is a counterintuitive note on which to win.
sentences.zh: 然后他停顿了一下说，许多尚未长大的男孩将因此而保住性命，这是一个反直觉的获胜基调。

sentences.en: On that, we will take a break and finish today's episode.
sentences.zh: 说到这里，我们要休息一下，结束今天的节目。

sentences.en: And we will be back with the second half of this story.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会回来讲述这个故事的下半部分。

sentences.en: So the way the atom bomb is used in Japan, Oppenheimer's views on that, all the kind of historiographical complexities around it, and then the story of Oppenheimer's downfall.
sentences.zh: 关于原子弹在日本的使用方式，奥本海默对此的看法，围绕它所有的史学复杂性，以及奥本海默最终垮台的故事。

sentences.en: And ultimately, he gets kind of rehabilitated, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 而且最终，他算是得到了平反，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 所以我们很快就会在第二部分见到你们，除非，当然，你是“历史余音”俱乐部的成员

sentences.zh: 所以我们要么，你知道，几分钟后再见，要么几天后再见。

sentences.zh: 不管怎样，再见。
